Skill patched. I added a section covering the generalizable structure this question exposed.

What was worth saving:
- The two-phase "find-the-extremum-month, then cross-table lookup" pattern — phase 1 scans a monthly series for a min/max, phase 2 uses that month as the key into a different table. This is a reusable question structure independent of the specific data.
- The data locations: yield spreads (corporate Aa minus Treasury bond yields) live in the Bulletin's interest-rate/yield section; trust-account receipts (railroad retirement, etc.) live in the budget receipts/trust-fund tables.
- The "named issue publishes a multi-year monthly history" insight — one issue (June 1970) covers the whole 1960-1969 scan, so you don't open ten issues.
- The unit/format convention: "full number without commas or words in nominal dollars" means expand a millions-table figure ("92") to its literal integer (92000000) — no rounding, no scaling to billions.
- The phase-1-error-propagates pitfall.

No memory update needed — the durable dataset facts are already captured, and this is procedural knowledge that belongs in the skill.
